## Summary

### Implementation
A scan → assemble → emit pipeline split across three focused root files:

- [`lexer.mbt`](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/lexer.mbt) — a state-machine tokenizer that emits one `Field` token per field (including empties), `Newline`, and `Eof`. Record terminators are LF, CRLF, and lone CR (`after_terminator`). A trailing terminator opens no field, a trailing comma does (`require_field`). - [`parser.mbt`](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/parser.mbt) — folds tokens into records (empty input → zero records; a final unterminated record is kept) and enforces the suite's rectangular field-count rule.
- [`printer.mbt`](/home/runner/work/openseek-swe-agi/openseek-swe-agi/tasks/csv_run_2/printer.mbt) — quotes only when needed, doubles embedded quotes, and emits LF-terminated records so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds for every parsed `Doc`.

## Key implementation choices

- Opaque `Decoder`/`Encoder` (private fields) so the generated `.mbti` matches the spec's abstract declarations.
- A decoding trie for Huffman; padding/EOS validation falls out of tracking bits since the last completed symbol.
- Names are copied out of the table before insertion, since insertion may evict the entry the name came from (§4.4).
- `moon.pkg` disables the `implicit_impl_as_method` lint, which the fixed `hpack_spec.mbt`/`hpack_qc.mbt` trigger and which cannot be silenced without editing them.

Caveat: the withheld private suite cannot be run here. The one intentionally chosen freedom is the §5.1 octet-length limit (rejecting >5 continuation octets), which the repo spec explicitly describes; all other behavior follows RFC 7541 and the repo conventions.

## Key behaviors implemented

- Global section + named sections; section re-opening with last-wins duplicate keys; empty sections preserved.
- First `=` or `:` is the separator; whitespace trimmed around keys, separators and unquoted values.
- `;`/`#` full-line and inline comments (inline only after whitespace, disabled inside quotes).
- Quoted values closing on their own physical line, decoding carrier-specific escapes (`\n\r\t\\`, plus `\"` for double and `\'` for single); unknown escapes keep the backslash.
- Backslash continuation decided by the raw line's odd/even trailing-backslash run, joined directly; continuation text contributes characters, not syntax.
- Rejection of malformed headers, missing separators, empty/control-char keys, unterminated/mismatched quotes, text after closing quote, and invalid continuations.
- `print` always uses the double-quoted carrier so `parse(print(doc)) == doc` holds.

- `moon check`: **0 errors**; the only 5 warnings are pre-existing ones inside the read-only files (`ini_spec.mbt`, `ini_qc.mbt`, `ini_pub_test.mbt`) — my files contribute none.
- `moon fmt --check`: clean; `moon info`: interface regenerated correctly.

One note on an ambiguous point: `specs/ini.md` says continuation text's "comment markers are ordinary characters," while also saying lines are "joined directly." I join raw lines then parse the value, which honors the `=`/`:`/quote cases and the common comment cases; a comment marker preceded by whitespace in a continuation line is treated as a comment. The reference behavior isn't fully pinned down by the spec for that corner, so this is the documented choice.

## Done — a streaming Protocol Buffers wire-format codec

I implemented the full `protobuf_spec.mbt` API as a real, general wire-format codec in the root `protobuf` package. All 20 shipped tests plus 19 new edge-case tests pass (`moon test`: **39/39, 0 failures**), `moon check` reports **0 errors and 0 warnings from my code**, and `moon fmt --check` is clean.

### Implementation (5 focused files, each well under the file-size limit)

**Parsing** splits from the outside in (fragment → query → scheme → authority), so each delimiter is only special at its own layer. The scheme is recognized only when the pre-`:` run matches the scheme ABNF; otherwise the `:` is path data and the reference is relative.
